from.place: Since the finite ring $\Lambda=P_n$ is annihilated by an integer, $F_{\Et}$ is a torsion abelian sheaf, so the classical input of the source note (Th. 1.1 of SGA 4 1/2 and [Tag 095U](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/095U)) applies to $f_{\Et}$: the sheaves $R^qf_{\Et,*}F_{\Et}$ are constructible and zero for $q>2e$.

title: Étale proper direct-image finiteness
statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme] which are Noetherian (each has a finite affine open cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]) and finite-dimensional (the Krull dimension of each underlying space [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] is bounded above by a nonnegative integer), let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] whose geometric fibres [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] have Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] at most $e\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, and let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring whose underlying set is finite whose element orders are invertible in every local ring of $Y$. For every constructible sheaf [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] $F$ of $\Lambda$-modules on the small étale site $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], the sheaves $R^qf_{\Et,*}F$ are constructible $\Lambda$-module sheaves on $Y_{\Et}$ for all integers $q\geq0$, and $R^qf_{\Et,*}F=0$ for every $q>2e$.

proof.text: The finite affine Noetherian covers make $X,Y$ locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Each covering affine has Noetherian underlying space by [lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space], hence is quasi-compact: otherwise finite partial unions of an open covering would yield a strictly increasing chain of opens. A finite union of these affines is quasi-compact, so $X,Y$ are quasi-compact. They are quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Properness gives separatedness and finite type [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. By [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth], $f$ is locally of finite presentation. It is also quasi-compact and quasi-separated (its diagonal is a closed immersion), hence of finite presentation. Finally $\Lambda$ is Noetherian: an ideal is a finite set, and is generated by all its elements. There is a positive integer $N$ with $N\cdot1_\Lambda=0$, since the additive sequence $0,1,2\cdot1,\ldots$ in a finite ring repeats; then $NM=0$ for every $\Lambda$-module $M$, including sections of every $\Lambda$-module sheaf.

source.place: Tag 0GL0 hypotheses; finite-ring and Noetherian-base specialization

proof.text: Use the identity compactification $(j,p)=(1_X,f)$ in [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification]. Its candidate is $Rf_* (1_X)_!$. For the identity open immersion every object $V\to X$ factors uniquely through $X$, so the presheaf defining $(1_X)_!F$ in [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] is exactly $F$ with its original restrictions; sheafification of this sheaf leaves it unchanged. Applying this degreewise gives $Rf_!^{(1_X,f)}K=Rf_*K$. Place $F$ in degree zero. Its only nonzero cohomology sheaf is $F$, so it is bounded below with constructible cohomology; the zero sheaves in the other degrees are locally constant with zero value on the one-stratum partition.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-compactification-constructibility] to $K=F[0]$ and the identity compactification, using the hypotheses checked in step 1. It gives constructibility of every $\mathcal H^q(Rf_*F)=R^qf_*F$, with the equality being the definition in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. This is the constructibility clause. No coefficient change and no replacement by a pro-etale category occurs.

Fix any geometric point $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ with image $y$. By [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-extension-embeds-algebraically-closed], embed an algebraic closure $\Omega_0=\overline{\kappa(y)}$ into the algebraically closed field $\Omega$ over $\kappa(y)$. Put $T=X_{\bar y}$ and $G=F|_T$. Since $f$ is separated and of finite type, [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change] makes $T$ a finite-type $\Omega$-scheme. The fibre $T_0=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_0$ has dimension at most $e$ by hypothesis, and $T=T_0\times_{\Omega_0}\Omega$. Apply [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change] to the finite-type structure morphism of $T_0$: each dimension at a point of $T$ equals that at its image in $T_0$, hence is at most $e$. This bounds $\dim T$ by $e$: for a chain of irreducible closed subsets, choose a point in its smallest member; every open neighbourhood of that point meets each successive difference, so the same chain restricts to a strict chain in every such neighbourhood. Thus its length is at most the dimension at that point. If $T$ is nonempty, put $d=\dim T$, so $0\leq d\leq e$. The algebraically closed field $\Omega$ is separably closed, so [lem-sf-separably-closed-torsion-cd] gives $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(\Omega)\leq0$. The underlying abelian sheaf of $G$ is killed by $N$ from step 1, so [thm-sc-finite-type-torsion-cd] and [def-sc-etale-torsion-cd] give $H^q_{\rm Ab}(T,G_{\rm Ab})=0$ for $q>2d$, in particular for $q>2e$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-module-cohomology-forget], the underlying group of $H^q_\Lambda(T,G)$ is this zero group, so $H^q_\Lambda(T,G)=0$. If $T$ is empty, its small etale site has only the empty scheme; the empty covering forces every module sheaf to have its zero module of sections, so its sheaf category and all these cohomology groups are zero as well.

source.place: Tag 095U, label lemma-cohomological-dimension-proper, reduction to geometric-fibre cohomology; general finite-type bound supplied by the cited DAG theorem

proof.text: For $K=F[0]$, [cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite] gives $\bar y^{-1}Rf_*F\cong Ra_{\bar y,*}G$. Here $C=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. By [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-cohomology], sections of an abelian sheaf on $C$ are naturally its stalk at $1_C$. Together with [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] this makes sections exact; for module sheaves the same follows because kernels, images and exactness are computed on underlying abelian sheaves. Exact stalks and sections commute with cohomology: apply [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology] to the cycles and boundaries of a representing complex. Thus the degree-$q$ sections of the left side are $(R^qf_*F)_{\bar y}$. To compute the right side, choose a bounded-below injective resolution $G\to I$ in module sheaves on $T$. The definition [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] represents $Ra_{\bar y,*}G$ by $a_{\bar y,*}I$. Its sections on $C$ are $I(T)$ degreewise, by the direct-image formula, so their degree-$q$ cohomology is $H^q_\Lambda(T,G)$. Hence $(R^qf_*F)_{\bar y}\cong H^q_\Lambda(T,G)$, which is zero for $q>2e$ by step 4. This uses the derived assertion of the fibre node, whose input is any bounded-below complex, and does not require $F$ to be globally locally constant.

source.place: Tag 095U proof, via proper-base-change geometric-fibre stalk formula

proof.text: Let $q>2e$ and write $A=R^qf_*F$ in the module category. By [lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-forget-comparison], its underlying abelian sheaf is the abelian higher direct image of the underlying abelian sheaf of $F$. Its geometric stalks at all geometric points vanish by step 5, with arbitrary algebraically closed overfields covered by the dimension check in step 4. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] to $0\to A_{\rm Ab}$: its stalk maps are all isomorphisms $0\to0$, hence $A_{\rm Ab}=0$. A module sheaf with zero underlying abelian sheaf has only its zero module on every site object, so $A=0$. This proves the vanishing clause.

lean.statement: theorem proper_directImage_finiteness {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian Y] (hXdim : ∃ d : ℕ, topologicalKrullDim X ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) (hYdim : ∃ d : ℕ, topologicalKrullDim Y ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f] (e : ℕ) (hfib : ∀ y : Y, topologicalKrullDim ↥(pullback f (Y.algClosurePoint y)) ≤ (e : WithBot ℕ∞)) (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] [Finite Λ] (hΛ : ∀ (a : Λ) (y : Y), IsUnit (addOrderOf a : Y.presheaf.stalk y)) (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)) (hF : Scheme.IsConstructibleEtaleModuleSheaf F) : (∀ q : ℤ, 0 ≤ q → Scheme.IsConstructibleEtaleModuleSheaf (higherDirectImage Λ f q F)) ∧ (∀ q : ℤ, (2 * e : ℤ) < q → IsZero (higherDirectImage Λ f q F))
